label: SFTP / FTP
explain: SFTP is a way computers share files securely over the internet. We'll log in to a folder and pick up new files as they arrive.
description: Poll files from an SFTP or FTP server

props.label: host
props.help: The address of the server that holds your files. Looks like a website name.

props.label: port
props.q: Which door do we use to log in?
props.help: Most SFTP servers use door 22. Use 21 for plain FTP. If unsure, leave it at 22.

props.label: username
props.help: Your username on the server. Your IT admin will know this.

props.label: password
props.help: Don't worry — this is stored as a secret reference, never as plain text in the generated code.

props.label: remote folder
props.help: The path to the folder on the server. Folders usually start with a slash, like /home/raj/incoming.

props.label: poll every
props.q: How often should we check for new files?
props.help: We'll peek into the folder on a schedule. More often = faster reactions, but more network traffic.

label: Timer
explain: A Timer kicks off your flow on a regular beat — every minute, every hour, every Monday at 9am. No external system needed.
description: Trigger a flow on a fixed time interval

props.label: every
props.help: Pick a beat. The flow will trigger on this schedule, like an alarm clock.

props.label: repeat count
props.q: How many times? (Leave blank for forever)
props.help: If you want this to run a fixed number of times (e.g. for testing), put a number here.

label: HTTP Endpoint
explain: An HTTP endpoint listens at a web address. When someone POSTs data to it, your flow runs with that data as the message.
description: Receive HTTP requests on a given path and port

props.label: path
props.help: The path part of the URL, like /orders. Your service will respond at this path.

props.label: port
props.help: Leave at 8080 unless you have a specific reason to change it.

props.label: method
props.help: POST is for sending in new data. GET is for asking for data back. Most integrations use POST.

label: File Watcher
explain: Watches a folder on this machine. Any file that lands in it becomes a message and flows through your route.
description: Watch a local directory for new files

props.label: folder
props.help: An absolute path on the local machine.

props.label: recursive
props.help: If your files end up in nested folders inside, choose yes.

props.label: file pattern
props.help: A regex pattern like .*\.xml means only .xml files. Leave blank for all files.

label: Kafka Consumer
explain: Kafka is a message highway. A consumer is your subscription to one lane (a topic). You'll receive every message published there.
description: Consume messages from a Kafka topic

props.label: topic
props.q: Which topic do you want to read?
props.help: Topics are like channel names — ask your data team for the right one.

props.label: brokers
props.help: A comma-separated list of host:port. Your data team has these.

props.label: consumer group
props.help: A label for your subscription. Two services with the same group share the work; different groups each see everything.

label: JMS / ActiveMQ
explain: JMS is a standard for message queues. ActiveMQ is a popular system that implements it. You'll receive messages sent to a queue or topic.
description: Consume messages from a JMS queue or topic (ActiveMQ / Artemis)

props.label: broker URL
props.help: The connection URL for the broker. Your infrastructure team will have this.

props.label: destination type
props.help: Queues distribute work; topics broadcast to everyone subscribed.

props.label: queue / topic name
props.help: The queue or topic name you want to listen on.

label: Filter
explain: A Filter is a gatekeeper. It checks each message against a rule and only lets through the ones that match.
description: Let messages through only if a condition is true

props.label: check
props.help: We can check the file name, or look inside the message itself.

props.label: rule
props.help: Examples: *.xml means anything ending in .xml. Or write plain English and we'll translate it.

label: Transform
explain: Reshapes your message from one format into another — like translating a letter from Spanish to English.
description: Change the message body using a Simple or Groovy expression

props.label: from
props.help: What format does the data come in as?

props.label: to
props.help: Pick the format your destination expects.

props.label: expression (advanced)
props.help: Leave blank if the from/to selection above is enough. For advanced cases, write a Camel Simple expression.

label: Split Records
explain: Takes a message that contains many items (like a list of orders) and splits it into one message per item — so the rest of the flow runs once per item.
description: Split the message into multiple parts

props.label: split by

options.title: One per line
options.sub: Each row on its own line

props.help: Pick the pattern that matches your data.

label: Log / Print
explain: Writes a line to the service's log file. Use this anywhere to see what's happening — it's the most reliable debugger you have.
description: Print the message or a custom text to the application log

props.label: level
props.help: Higher levels show up in production by default; DEBUG is hidden unless you turn it on.

props.label: message
props.help: Type a sentence. Use ${body} to drop in the message content, or ${header.foo} for headers.

label: REST Call
explain: Makes a web request to another system in the middle of your flow — useful when you need to enrich data or notify an external service.
description: Call an external REST API with configurable method, headers, and query params

props.label: URL
props.help: Include the https:// part.

props.label: method
props.help: POST creates, PUT updates, GET reads.

props.label: headers (JSON)
props.help: Leave blank for no headers. Format: {"Header-Name": "value"}

label: XSLT Transform
explain: XSLT is a language for transforming XML. If someone hands you an .xsl file, this block applies it to every message that passes through.
description: Apply an XSLT stylesheet to transform XML messages

props.label: stylesheet path
props.help: Usually a classpath reference like classpath:transform.xsl — put the file in src/main/resources.

label: JSON ↔ XML Convert
explain: Automatically converts the message body between JSON and XML. Useful when your source speaks JSON but your destination wants XML, or vice versa.
description: Convert message body between JSON and XML formats

props.label: direction
props.help: JSON is curly-brace format. XML is tag-based.

label: Send Email
explain: Sends an email. Good for alerts to humans — not for high-volume data movement.
description: Send the message body as an email

props.label: to
props.help: An email address. You can use commas for multiple people.

props.label: subject
props.help: You can include parts of the message with ${body} or ${header.name}.

props.label: SMTP host
props.help: Your SMTP server address. Gmail is smtp.gmail.com, Outlook is smtp.office365.com.

props.label: SMTP port
props.help: 587 for TLS (recommended), 465 for SSL, 25 for plain (not recommended).

props.label: username
props.help: Used to authenticate with the mail server.

props.label: password
props.help: Stored as a secret. For Gmail, use an App Password, not your main password.

label: Save to DB
explain: Saves the message into a row in a database table. We assume the message is already shaped right (use a Transform first if not).
description: Execute a SQL statement with the message body as input

props.label: table
props.help: The table to write into.

props.label: mode
props.help: Insert always adds a new row. Upsert updates if it exists, inserts if not.

props.label: JDBC URL
props.help: Your database connection string. Starts with jdbc:postgresql:// for Postgres or jdbc:mysql:// for MySQL.

label: Kafka Topic
explain: Publishes the message onto a Kafka topic, where any number of other services can pick it up.
description: Publish messages to a Kafka topic

props.label: topic
props.q: Which topic should we publish to?
props.help: Topics are like channel names.

props.label: brokers
props.help: host:port pairs separated by commas.

label: HTTP Call
explain: Makes a web request to another system — like calling a Stripe webhook or a partner's API.
description: POST the message body to an HTTP endpoint

props.label: url
props.help: Include the https:// part.

props.label: method
props.help: POST creates, PUT updates, GET reads.

label: Logger
explain: Sends the message to your application's log (the same place Spring Boot prints startup lines). Use this as a simple sink to verify a flow or debug payloads.
description: Log the message body to a named logger

props.label: logger name
props.q: What should we call this logger?
props.help: Shows up in log output so you can filter lines, e.g. flowcamel or orders.pipeline.

props.label: level
props.q: How important is this log line?
props.help: INFO is typical for completed steps; use DEBUG while building the flow.

label: JMS / ActiveMQ Producer
explain: Sends the message to a JMS queue or topic. The mirror image of the JMS source.
description: Send messages to a JMS queue or topic (ActiveMQ / Artemis)

props.label: broker URL
props.help: The connection URL for the broker.

props.label: destination type
props.help: Queues distribute work; topics broadcast to everyone subscribed.

props.label: queue / topic name
props.help: The queue or topic name to send to.
